searchText: Goerli forking in ~40 minutes. If anyone wants to join the watch party, you can do so here: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/81324137308?pwd=Eb3PEKAXU0vzaCN3nLWziv9WOUZlFc.1 Streamed here: https://youtube.com/live/jbhFdUFnWUU?feature=share But it's the middle of the afternoon? What kind of time is this for a hard fork? 😄 Love upgrades in Australian day time. <@&595681804422479873> did y'all forget to update your goerli nodes? in theory no, it was recorded as having been done Got it -- saw some missed blocks tagged `Nimbus` on beaconcha.in, see: https://goerli.beaconcha.in/validator/174151#blocks as an example. Might be a mistaken tag! Also showing some missed ones by Prysm (https://goerli.beaconcha.in/validator/46114#blocks) looks like at least one node is opt-synced, won't do validator duties as a result so Nimbus synced but it thinks EL isn't (true or false or why don't know) Do you have some logs for the EL? sure, conveniently looks like it's geth (`ethereum/client-goethereum/client-go`) ``` WARN [01-17|07:13:36.674] Served engine_newPayloadV3 conn=172.17.9.1:56576 reqid=31538 duration="348.392µs" err="Unsupported fork" errdata="{Error:newPayloadV3 called pre-cancun}" WARN [01-17|07:13:36.941] Forkchoice requested unknown head hash=c96d7c..402777 WARN [01-17|07:13:42.086] Served debug_metrics reqid=1 duration="8.527µs" err="the method debug_metrics does not exist/is not available" WARN [01-17|07:13:50.194] Served engine_newPayloadV3 conn=172.17.9.1:55548 reqid=31541 duration=2.652929ms err="Unsupported fork" errdata="{Error:newPayloadV3 called pre-cancun}" WARN [01-17|07:13:50.465] Forkchoice requested unknown head hash=ae664d..f4ad15 WARN [01-17|07:14:01.432] Served engine_newPayloadV3 conn=172.17.9.1:55790 reqid=31544 duration="216.058µs" err="Unsupported fork" errdata="{Error:newPayloadV3 called pre-cancun}" WARN [01-17|07:14:01.701] Forkchoice requested unknown head hash=b53e53..09d03c WARN [01-17|07:14:12.086] Served debug_metrics reqid=1 duration="8.486µs" err="the method debug_metrics does not exist/is not available" WARN [01-17|07:14:14.613] Served engine_newPayloadV3 conn=172.17.9.1:43258 reqid=31547 duration="662.087µs" err="Unsupported fork" errdata="{Error:newPayloadV3 called pre-cancun}" W ``` welp v1.13.8 looks like someone forgot to update 😄 https://discord.com/channels/613988663034118151/641680546191376384/1195382787742634045 (Nimbus Discord server) and https://discord.com/channels/613988663034118151/641680546191376384/1194928958265892885 says Geth was updated to v1.13.9 weeks ago but guess not couldn't have been weeks ago, as v1.13.9 was released not even a week ago. 5:30 PM CEST Jan 10 oh right, Jan 11 days ago anyway, definitely in the past and not the future some Nimbus fleet servers did get updated to v1.13.9, but others did not Could you update to 1.13.10? The .9 release was a bit botched sure, relayed that information at least update to v1.13.10 in process four of Nimbus Goerli nodes have recovered and are synced, attesting, etc. 3 nodes, all v1.13.10, are responding as SYNCING I've published a small benchmark suite based on my EVM fractal generator stuff. I really don't know how to add other clients and I'm unsure I would find the time to figure it out, but PRs are welcome; ideally via some docker method so I don't have to build 6 different ecosystems. https://github.com/karalabe/burntpix-benchmark Even if nobody wants to be listed, the code is very math and compute heavy, so it might be an interesting thing to profile and see if there are some low hanging fruits to optimise in one client or another Thought about this over lunch and I removed all notions of client comparisons. Everyone is welcome to use the code as a stress test for their own client to optimise, but I don't want to start a measuring contest. Keeping it positive rather: enjoy the pics while tuning your code. **ACDE tomorrow 14:00 UTC** Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/939 Stream: https://youtube.com/live/FhMBatolkOM Zoom will be shared here right before the call. A few notes about tomorrow's call: - First, great work everyone on triaging and fixing the issues found on Goerli yesterday 🙌 ! The current set dates for Sepolia (Jan 30) & Holesky (Feb 7) assume that we put out client releases and an announcement by mid next week. **If, due to how Goerli went yesterday, teams feel like this is too soon, we absolutely need to decide on tomorrow's call. ** Regardless, as <@583892532644151312> pointed out, we should at least get the 4788 contracts deployed on Sepolia and Holesky (maybe we want to wait for mainnet?). - Second, we're planning to review the various Prague/Electra proposals, so please have a look at the thread before the call (https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/prague-electra-network-upgrade-meta-thread/16809). Shoutout to <@&1070471163219824730> for writing up their views ahead of time: https://www.paradigm.xyz/2024/01/ethereum-2024 ! - Third, on the next ACDE (Feb 1), we'd like to do a deep dive into Verkle, given how big it is. It would be useful for the Verkle folks if tomorrow we could aggregate questions/topics/etc. that people would like to cover, so that they can prepare accordingly. See you tomorrow! Just add to https://github.com/ziyadedher/evm-bench or https://github.com/ipsilon/evm-benchmarks <@892053833121923094> deployed the contract to Sepolia and Holesky 🔥 https://holesky.etherscan.io/tx/0xdf52c2d3bbe38820fff7b5eaab3db1b91f8e1412b56497d88388fb5d4ea1fde0 https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0xdf52c2d3bbe38820fff7b5eaab3db1b91f8e1412b56497d88388fb5d4ea1fde0 Will ping Ziyad to add Wrote up a summary of why we should ship either 3074 or 5806 in next hardfork: https://0xfoobar.substack.com/p/batch-transactions-for-eoas TLDR: - stale approvals are a huge security risk, have already drained 100s of millions from retail. EOA batch txs fix this - batch txs are a 'free lunch' for state growth, by removing unnecessary overhead of sequential txs can fit more actions into same state size - batch txs eliminate unbundling risk and make the private relaying world more competitive - EOAs are >90% of current addresses, should continue improving the default experience while working on more complex smart contract wallets Will cross-post another write up from the agenda, by <@418000431814279181>, about `SETCODE`: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1fUsgZmfTwH59rr8Ca7MK2xSaDLgkHXhjBQk-AnP31_g/edit#slide=id.p

excerpts.author: foobar0x
excerpts.content:
Wrote up a summary of why we should ship either 3074 or 5806 in next hardfork: https://0xfoobar.substack.com/p/batch-transactions-for-eoas

TLDR:
- stale approvals are a huge security risk, have already drained 100s of millions from retail. EOA batch txs fix this
- batch txs are a 'free lunch' for state growth, by removing unnecessary overhead of sequential txs can fit more actions into same state size
- batch txs eliminate unbundling risk and make the private relaying world more competitive
- EOAs are >90% of current addresses, should continue improving the default experience while working on more complex smart contract wallets
